suites.title: Core regression
suites.description: No response-header dependency. Generic meta, unrelated bots and link rules.

suites.title: HTML meta
suites.description: Independent noindex/nofollow behavior and parsing edge cases.

suites.title: HTTP headers
suites.description: Real response headers must be configured before this run.

suites.title: robots.txt switch
suites.description: Run twice with fresh state: Ignore robots.txt OFF, then ON.

suites.title: Confirmed-token tests
suites.description: Requires the exact supported SearchStax meta-name mapping.

suites.title: Contract decisions
suites.description: Exploratory only until the behavior is agreed.

cases.title: Empty separators surrounding valid tokens
cases.note: Robustness expectation: empty comma-separated tokens have no meaning; valid tokens must still apply.

cases.title: Unknown token beside valid noindex
cases.note: Unknown token must not cause valid noindex to be discarded or the crawl to fail.

cases.title: Missing content attribute
cases.note: Malformed-input robustness: no crash, and no unsupported restriction should be invented.

cases.title: Directive substrings are not tokens
cases.note: Exact token matching only. These strings are not noindex or nofollow.

cases.title: Robots tag inside an HTML comment
cases.note: A commented-out tag is not an active head element.

cases.title: Robots meta in body, not head
cases.note: Ticket-specific head-only expectation. This is not a claim about Google, which may honor body tags. Verify against raw response HTML, not a repaired browser DOM.

cases.title: http-equiv is not a real HTTP header
cases.note: No response X-Robots-Tag exists. This is neither a name=robots tag nor the HTTP-header feature in the ticket.

cases.title: Separate generic meta tags
cases.note: Ticket does not specify aggregation across multiple tags. Proposed decision: combine restrictions to noindex + nofollow. Do not report a defect until agreed.

cases.title: Conflicting directives in one meta tag
cases.note: Conflict precedence is not defined in the ticket. Proposed decision: restrictive wins; confirm before pass/fail.

cases.title: The none shorthand is outside explicit scope
cases.note: Ask whether none (a common alias for noindex,nofollow) is supported. The ticket only requires noindex and nofollow.

cases.title: googlebot-only directives must not apply
cases.note: Run with a confirmed non-Googlebot SearchStax crawler identity.

cases.title: An unrelated bot name is ignored
Generic noindex survives unrelated bot allow
Matching configured bot: noindex
cases.note: Applies only after the exact supported meta-name mapping is confirmed; current token is configurable.

cases.title: Matching bot name and directive case
Specific allow overrides generic block
cases.note: Expected per this ticket: the supported specific tag takes precedence. Do not substitute Google-style restriction merging.

cases.title: Specific precedence is independent of tag order
Specific tag specifies only one dimension
cases.note: Clarify whole-tag replacement versus per-directive override. With specific index, should the generic nofollow remain?

cases.title: Partial bot-name match is not enough
cases.note: Verify supported name mapping, not a substring of the HTTP User-Agent. This lookalike must not match unless explicitly registered.

cases.title: Mixed-case HTTP field name
cases.note: A CDN may normalize field-name case. The local server preserves this wire casing; behavior must remain case-insensitive.

cases.title: Repeated X-Robots-Tag field lines
cases.note: Clarify aggregation. Local server emits two physical field lines. Static CDNs may combine them; verify raw GET response before claiming the repeated-field variant was tested.

cases.title: Text document: restricted and allowed controls
cases.note: The parent has no restriction. Both text URLs are fetchable. Restricted text must not index, while allowed text must index. Establish .txt support first; otherwise mark Blocked, not Passed.

cases.title: Header noindex plus meta nofollow
cases.note: Cross-source merge behavior is not explicit. Proposed: apply both independent restrictions; obtain product confirmation.

cases.title: Header block versus meta allow
cases.note: Header-versus-meta conflict precedence requires a decision.

cases.title: Meta block versus header allow
cases.note: Reverse of H10; confirm the same deterministic conflict policy.

cases.title: Bot-scoped header for googlebot
cases.note: Bot-scoped HTTP header syntax is not explicitly promised by this ticket. Proposed: ignore this scope for a non-Googlebot crawler.

cases.title: Bot-scoped header for configured bot
cases.note: Confirm support for bot-scoped HTTP headers and exact token mapping before grading.

cases.title: Misspelled response header is not X-Robots-Tag
cases.note: Exact field-name match is required; the pluralized custom field does not impose page restrictions.

cases.title: One nofollow link and one normal link
Mixed case, tabs and newlines in rel
nofollowish is not a nofollow token
cases.note: Target slug says restricted for fixture consistency, but this occurrence must be eligible.

cases.title: Same URL: nofollow occurrence comes first
cases.note: The permitted occurrence can enqueue the URL. Assert one unique indexed URL, not exactly one physical request: retries are possible.

cases.title: Same URL: permitted occurrence comes first
cases.note: A later nofollow occurrence must not remove a URL legitimately queued from the earlier occurrence.

cases.title: Alternate permitted path reaches the same target
cases.note: Graph: parent -nofollow-> shared; parent -> bridge -> shared. The bridge makes shared eligible.

cases.title: Page nofollow is not a global URL blacklist
cases.note: Seed links to both source pages. Both source pages link to shared; the allowed source can enqueue it. This also detects state leaking from one page to another.

cases.title: noindex parent with mixed link-level rules
Page nofollow overrides an unrestricted link
cases.note: rel=follow does not cancel page-level nofollow; neither occurrence may enqueue a child.

cases.title: Multiple fragment occurrences are all nofollow
cases.note: Fragments do not create an unrestricted occurrence. Do not seed shared directly.

cases.title: Comma is not a rel-token separator
cases.note: HTML rel is a whitespace-separated token list, unlike comma-or-whitespace robots content. Here the sole token is nofollow,external, not nofollow.

cases.title: robots.txt block with no page directive
cases.note: Run in two fresh crawls. Ignore robots.txt OFF: blocked parent is not fetched and no child is discovered from it. ON: fetch parent, then apply the page directives shown here. Seed is the allowed case entry, not the blocked page.

cases.title: robots.txt block plus noindex
cases.note: Run in two fresh crawls. Ignore robots.txt OFF: blocked parent is not fetched and no child is discovered from it. ON: fetch parent, then apply the page directives shown here. Seed is the allowed case entry, not the blocked page.

cases.title: robots.txt block plus nofollow
cases.note: Run in two fresh crawls. Ignore robots.txt OFF: blocked parent is not fetched and no child is discovered from it. ON: fetch parent, then apply the page directives shown here. Seed is the allowed case entry, not the blocked page.

cases.title: robots.txt block plus both directives
cases.note: Run in two fresh crawls. Ignore robots.txt OFF: blocked parent is not fetched and no child is discovered from it. ON: fetch parent, then apply the page directives shown here. Seed is the allowed case entry, not the blocked page.

cases.title: robots.txt ignore does not bypass link nofollow
cases.note: OFF: blocked parent is not fetched. ON: parent indexes; only its normal link may enqueue a child. Child paths themselves are allowed by robots.txt.

cases.title: robots.txt ignore does not bypass response headers
cases.note: OFF: blocked parent is not fetched. ON: parent is fetched but not indexed, and neither links nor children are queued from it.

cases.title: Existing document: add/remove meta noindex
cases.note: Same parent URL in baseline V1, restricted V2, restored V3. Seed V1 first. Under noindex, V2 must not be added or update the existing document. Whether V1 is retained or removed is an open product decision; do not assert deletion. Restore directives and verify V3 indexes. Use a forced/full re-fetch; record any independent stale-document cleanup policy.

cases.title: Existing document: add/remove header noindex
cases.note: Same parent URL in baseline V1, restricted V2, restored V3. Seed V1 first. Under noindex, V2 must not be added or update the existing document. Whether V1 is retained or removed is an open product decision; do not assert deletion. Restore directives and verify V3 indexes. Use a forced/full re-fetch; record any independent stale-document cleanup policy.

cases.title: Add page nofollow before introducing a new child
cases.note: Baseline links only old-child. Restricted V2 introduces new-child while setting page nofollow: new-child must not be queued. Old-child may already exist; do not use its presence as failure evidence. Restored V3 removes nofollow and permits both children.

cases.title: Add link nofollow before introducing a new child
cases.note: Baseline exposes old-child only. Restricted V2 exposes new-child only through a nofollow link: old-child remains eligible, new-child must not be queued. Restored V3 removes the new-child rel restriction.
